title: Table tops, bases and joints
intro: A table is a system of top, base and connections. Trace load paths, coordinate material interfaces and identify the evidence needed to review stability and performance.
goals: Define the top and support relationship

sections.title: Define the top and support relationship
sections.text: Record the top material, build-up, grain direction where relevant, edges, use and cleaning needs. A fixing detail cannot simply transfer between solid timber, faced board and stone. A section should identify top, support, connection and unsupported projection. An apparent thick edge may be an applied detail; appearance does not establish structural thickness.
sections.caption: Identify the actual build-up before selecting the interface.

sections.title: Trace loads and compare bases
sections.text: Trace load from top through frame or pedestal to floor contacts. A central base changes edge projections, while perimeter legs affect seating. A load-path sketch is not proof of adequacy. Define expected loading, edge use, sway, twisting and floor conditions for an appropriate technical review; do not improvise testing by standing on the table or adding arbitrary loads.
sections.caption: The load path defines the review; it does not certify capacity.

sections.title: Review connections, movement and disassembly
sections.text: Identify permanent/removable connections, tool access and material movement the system must accommodate. Solid timber dimensions can change with humidity; do not assume rigid restraint in every direction. Obtain a suitable manufacturer/specialist detail. In an exercise with a 1600 mm top and centered 1000 mm base length, each end projects ⁦(1600 − 1000) ÷ 2 = 300⁩ mm; this does not validate the projection structurally.
sections.caption: 300 mm is geometric projection, not a capacity approval.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: The solid-timber top on a metal base has a 300 mm exercise projection at each end, but the drawing specifies rigid attachment without explaining movement accommodation. Return the interface for review and require the connection, movement and tool-access detail before manufacture.
example.decision: Decision: complete the movement/connection detail and performance review.

quiz.question: What does the 300 mm projection calculation establish?
quiz.explanation: Performance requires review of the complete system.

assignment.prompt: Submit a top/base section, load path, connection/disassembly detail, projection calculation and verification requirements.

faq.question: Is the apparent edge thickness enough to choose a connection?
faq.answer: No. It may be an applied edge; obtain the actual section, material and build-up.
